EZ Flash Jr Patcher

Each file is checked against the known stock hashes before anything is patched, and the result is checked again before you can save it. Source and docs: github.com/lukesau/ezgb.

Kernel Safe option

The kernel is the ezgb.dat file on your microSD card. Stock files come from EZ Flash: the 1.04e / FW4 package on their download page (EZ-FLASH Junior), or the 1.05e FW5 2021-9-18 package.

Firmware updater Experimental
THIS CAN BRICK YOUR CART.

The patched updater rewrites the bootloader (stage1) in the cart's FPGA flash, as an official firmware update does, with the same risk. A bitstream that fails its CRC is caught by the cart's own fallback image, but a bootloader that runs and then hangs cannot be fixed with another updater: recovery needs hardware, an SPI programmer on the flash chip or JTAG. This firmware has run on one FW4 and one FW5 Jr. Only flash it if you accept losing the cart.

Use a fast, good-quality microSD card and fresh batteries (or a plugged-in, charging console), and do not power off while the updater writes. EZ Flash's FW5 is itself a release candidate: on slow SD cards it can halt at LOADING or OS INIT. If you don't need what the firmware adds, use the kernel above and stop there.

What it adds: a new boot screen, fast launch straight from the bootloader (the game named by FLAUNCH= in /EZGB.CFG, START at power-on cancels), the pending save backed up before a fast launch (never when the battery is dead), Super Game Boy detection (untested on a real Super Game Boy; it takes over from the kernel's SGB BOOT box, which is tested, so on an SGB use the kernel alone for now), and on FW5 the MBC3 game clock and fast loading.

Installing:

  1. Install the kernel above first.
  2. Copy the patched updater to the card, launch it from the file browser like a game, and press A. Wait until it says it's done.
  3. Power off and on. The boot screen's bottom line reads FW4-MOD or FW5-MOD and the mod's version.

Going back: run EZ Flash's official updater for your firmware the same way.
